review_summary: The junior differential captures the dominant renal pathology and its major complications, but probability weighting needs refinement and several critical laboratory and clinical data are missing. Adjusted probabilities better reflect the evidence hierarchy, and targeted investigations (BP, mineral‑bone labs, cardiovascular assessment, anemia work‑up, sleep study) are required to move several plausible diagnoses into the supported category.
